title: "Confidence interval"

  lang: en

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(exams)
library(mathml)
library(htmltools)
library(mistakes)

hook(n, N)
hook(p, P)
hook(quant, z)

task <- "confint1"
plfile <- file.path("rexams", sprintf("%s.pl", task))
rolog::consult(system.file(plfile, package="mistakes"))

source("utility.R")

## DATA GENERATION
repeat
{
  mu <- 100
  sigma <- 15
  n <- as.integer(round(runif(1, min=25, max=50)))
  perc <- sample(c(50, 80, 90, 95), 1)
  p <- perc / 100
  Q <- quote(search(confint1, confint1(mu, sigma, n, p), .S, .R, .P, .E))
  S <- findall(Q, options=list(preproc=as.rolog), env=environment())

  if(problems(S))
    next

  break
}

t <- prepare(task=task, S)
sol <- format_feedback(t$correct, t$explanations, t$bugs, t$praise, t$blame, t$extra)
```

Question
========

IQ scores in the general population are approximately normally distributed, 
with expectation $\mu=100$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma=15$. 
For this exercise, assume that IQ scores at a particular school follow the same distribution.
If we repeatedly draw samples of $N=`r n`$ from this school, 
between which two values do the central $`r perc`\%$ of the sample means fall?

```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The `r perc`%-confidence interval is calculated by: `r t$solution`

```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
sol <- lapply(sol, FUN=gsub, pattern="\\n", replacement="")
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
